content: Phosphatidylinositol N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase subunit Q, commonly referred to as PIG-Q, is an enzyme in humans that is encoded by the PIGQ gene. This gene plays a critical role in the initial step of glycosylphosphatidylinositol (GPI) anchor biosynthesis. The GPI anchor is a type of glycolipid that is present on the surface of many blood cells. Its primary function is to tether proteins to the cell membrane, ensuring their proper localization and function. The PIGQ gene encodes a component of the N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase enzyme complex. This complex is responsible for catalyzing the transfer of N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) from UDP-GlcNAc to phosphatidylinositol (PI), a key step in the formation of the GPI anchor. In terms of molecular interactions, PIG-Q has been demonstrated to interact with other proteins involved in the GPI biosynthesis pathway, including PIG-H, PIG-A, and PIG-C. These interactions are essential for the proper assembly and function of the enzyme complex.
